title: Direct goal manipulation through the unauthenticated admin goals endpoint
summary: The agent's objectives are replaced for every later invoice from every vendor until someone resets the configuration. High-value invoices are approved for payment without review.

LC.rationale: Unauthenticated POST /api/admin/finbot/goals stores attacker natural language unvalidated, and get_system_prompt appends it under CUSTOM GOALS (OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING) on the tool-choice path. That is a direct, unmediated language path into approve_invoice, not document ingestion or a closed-field transform.

CP.rationale: custom_goals is written to the FinBotConfig database row and injected into every later invoice run, while each invoice starts a fresh message list. That durable text changes standing behaviour after the originating request ends, so it is cross-session context rather than mere re-retrieval.

AP.rationale: The lab is a single FinBot agent with no handoffs; injected goals only relay from config into that agent's prompt and its own tools. Downstream invoice writes are subsequent-system impact, not a cross into another agent, tenant, or policy domain.

RH.rationale: Flag text is awarded inside approval code, but the packet has no human-verified episode of the agent gaming an evaluator, grader, or reward channel, and the repo has no tests confirming isolation. Whether that flag side effect is a reachable proxy cannot be decided from the prose walkthrough.

ES.rationale: The five tools are fixed in code with no dynamic tools, MCP servers, plugins, or skills, so the binding is allowlisted. Arguments are only JSON-parsed, and approve_invoice has no amount check, confirmation, or detector-flag gate, which are material schema and operation gaps.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice assistant whose system prompt carries the goals and whose loop ends on a model-selected approve, reject, or review tool call. That is the same model-directed action selection the profile describes, not a fixed policy engine.
